# TV role and Miracast

Modules: `nixos/modules/nixos/bcl/role/tv.nix` and `tvMiracast.nix`. Read [bcl-nixos](../bcl-nixos/SKILL.md) and [bcl-host-debugging](../bcl-host-debugging/SKILL.md) first. TV hosts are physical boxes: no deploy without approval, and Miracast must be treated as experimental per host.

## Kiosk (labwc + jellyfin-desktop)

- The app runs as user `tv` (own home): read its files with `sudo cat`. Its debug log is `~/.config/jellyfin-desktop/jellyfin-desktop.log`; `grep 'Window size:'` proves whether a resize/fullscreen request took effect. `settings.json` keys: `serverUrl`, `hwdec`, `audioPassthrough`, `windowWidth/windowHeight` (physical), `windowLogicalWidth/Height`, `windowMaximized`, `windowDecorations` (`csd`|`server`|`serverThemed`), `deviceName`, `hideScrollbar`.
- jellyfin-desktop is one native Wayland toplevel owned by mpv; CEF is an overlay. Its in-page titlebar hides only on a real xdg fullscreen state change delivered after startup. `windowMaximized` fills the screen but does not hide it.
- labwc `windowRule` actions fire once on first map; there is no "set fullscreen" action (only the `ToggleFullscreen` toggle) and the rule never took effect for this app. Prefer having the client request what it can do natively.
- Working fullscreen recipe: write the detected output size (`wlr-randr`) into `windowWidth/windowHeight` so mpv boots at the native resolution (the default boot geometry is 1600x900 and was never resynced); do NOT set `fullscreen=yes` in `mpv.conf` (the initial property value is consumed before the playback coordinator exists, so the page never gets `_nativeFullscreenChanged(true)` and the titlebar stays); instead set `input-ipc-server=/tmp/<name>.sock` in `mpv.conf`, background the app, wait for the log marker `starting Rust-owned mpv event thread`, then send `{"command":["set_property","fullscreen",true]}` through `socat - UNIX-CONNECT:<sock>`. The script ends with `wait "$pid"` so the session still blocks on the app.
- Hide decorations through the client (`windowDecorations: "csd"` makes mpv set `border=no`) rather than labwc server decorations, which a client can renegotiate.
- Cursor hiding: `cursorHideTimeout` is not a labwc option (unknown rc.xml elements are silently ignored). Use `swayidle` (works through `ext-idle-notifier-v1`) as a user service: on idle write `~/.config/labwc/environment.d/idle-cursor.env` with `XCURSOR_THEME=<transparent theme>` and `pkill -HUP -x labwc`; on resume remove it. The transparent theme is built with `xcursorgen` from a 1x1 PNG, with symlinks for all cursor-shape names. `environment.d/` stays writable because home-manager only symlinks the files it manages.
- Audio at boot: `pactl info` only proves the server is up. Wait until `pactl get-default-sink` is non-empty, then retry `pactl set-sink-volume` in a loop (HDMI sink creation races with EDID detection). Software volume in mpv is independent of the sink volume. A quiet TV with a healthy PipeWire chain (sink running, unmuted, mpv uncorked) is usually a TV-side or HDMI-CEC volume change.
- A `set -x` log without `set -e` shows failures but continues: grep the command's own stderr, do not trust "no crash".
- Handy: screenshot as the session user (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/<uid> WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0 grim`), then downscale before viewing (originals are huge); `pkill -f '[m]pv --fs'` (bracket trick) so the ssh command does not match itself; compare `readlink -f /nix/var/nix/profiles/system` across turns to see whether a deploy happened; a TV box on DHCP can change IP: run `hostname` after ssh before diagnosing, and refresh host keys only after the maintainer confirms.

## Miracast (miraclecast, P2P)

First check hardware: `iw list` "Supported interface modes" must contain `P2P-client` and `P2P-GO`. Without them (e.g. an RTL8821CE with `rtw88_8821ce`) the TV never appears on the phone: `miracle-wifid` logs `wpa_supplicant or driver does not support P2P` and `supplicant_p2p_start_scan()` errors every 15 s; not fixable in config (use a second, P2P-capable adapter). Nothing validates this at build time.

- Concurrent STA + P2P on one radio is experimental (upstream issue still open). Intel AX201 lists `managed` with `P2P-client, P2P-GO`, but P2P GO on 5 GHz is refused by wpa_supplicant (`forced channel for GO is not supported for P2P uses`, band-wide, a known iwlwifi issue): group stays on 2.4 GHz, so STA on 5 GHz plus P2P on 2.4 GHz means multi-channel time-slicing and choppy video even with idle CPU/GPU. Do NOT run `p2p_group_add freq=<5GHz>` on the live radio: it killed the network and needed two physical power cycles. Before any experiment touching P2P on the same radio, start `journalctl -f -u miraclecast-wifid > /tmp/x.log &` on the host so the log survives, and afterwards check `journalctl --list-boots`.
- Enabling the role froze one host on boot repeatedly (progressively earlier, no panic in the log). Disabling it fixed it; the root cause was never found. After enabling on a new host, verify several consecutive reboots.
- NetworkManager forces `networking.useDHCP = false`, which disables the dhcpcd service entirely: unmanaging the Wi-Fi interface from NetworkManager needs `networking.useDHCP = lib.mkForce true` besides `dhcpcd.allowInterfaces = [ "wl*" ]`, or the host loses all network.
- NixOS patches `wpa_cli` to use the client socket dir `/run/wpa_supplicant/client`, created only by the system `wpa_supplicant.service` (and only with `userControlled.enable`). That directory belongs to another unit's `RuntimeDirectory`, which systemd wipes whenever that unit restarts: re-run `mkdir -p` at the top of every iteration of the reconciliation loop, not only in `ExecStartPre`.
- Reconciliation scripts under `set -eu` must guard every `wpa_cli` call with `|| true`: an unguarded `add_network="$(cmd)"` crash-looped the service, and since it crashed right when P2P group formation started, the later channel-forcing code never ran (symptom was video lag, not a restarting service).
- Interface detection must skip `p2p-*` interfaces (virtual group interfaces `p2p-<if>-N` sort before the real one and appear only during a cast; the bug shows only mid-cast).
- `miracle-sinkctl` must be started with `run <interface>`: link labels are ifindex-based (`link/_<N>`), so an ini `autocmd=run 1` silently matches nothing while the service looks healthy (check `busctl` link properties `WfdSubelements`/`P2PScanning`).
- The default NixOS firewall drops the phone's DHCP discover on the group interface (connect, then disconnect after about 30 s): `networking.firewall.interfaces."p2p-+".allowedUDPPorts = [ 67 ]` (iptables `+` is a prefix wildcard).
- `FriendlyName` over D-Bus can diverge from the real supplicant state (shown as `unknown` on the phone): set `wpa_cli set device_name <hostname>` in the loop and verify with `wpa_cli get device_name`, not only `busctl get-property`.
- Phone does not list the TV while `P2PScanning` is false: `wpa_cli -p /run/miracle/wifi -i <if> p2p_find` revives it; the keepalive timer should re-arm it by itself within 15 s (if it recurs without manual interference, investigate the keepalive).
- Fullscreen of the cast window: do not set `waylandsink fullscreen=true` (the property is applied before the window exists and kills the whole `gst-launch` process, video and audio). Use a compositor rule on the app id `gst-launch-1.0` (sway `for_window ... fullscreen enable`).
- A frozen last frame after the phone stops casting is normal: `udpsrc` never signals EOS, teardown happens only on `AP-STA-DISCONNECTED`/`P2P-GROUP-REMOVED`, which can lag minutes behind the phone UI. Investigate only if `Connected` stays true much longer.
- `miracle-wifid` does not remove the P2P group interface after a failed attempt; retries fail with `Could not set interface p2p-...: Device or resource busy`. Clear with `wpa_cli ... p2p_group_remove <ifname>`, or restart `miraclecast-wifid` then `miraclecast-sinkctl`, in that order.
- `network.ssid` is optional: when unset, candidate SSIDs are taken from `networking.wireless.<ssid>.password` keys of the global secret file plus `bcl.global.networking.wireless`, each injected as a separate network (checked by SSID in `wpa_cli list_networks`, not by id 0).
- Branch hygiene: a fix for a bcl module consumed through a flake input must target the branch that the consumer's input (`bclOverrides`, override inputs) really points to now: check the consumer's `flake.nix` before committing or pushing, branches get merged and deleted.
